_spec.purpose: A standalone web edition of the archived visual story.
_spec.law: Facts resolve to the original verified claim record. A layout rebuild does not reverify reporting.

dek.text: Austin Community College says it is writing what it calls its first-ever AI policy. Its AI site already links a use policy for faculty and staff. The post names no vote.

introduction.text: [Austin Community College says it is developing an AI policy in alignment with its newly launched TRUST framework](c1). [Its post says the framework is meant to help shape what it calls its first-ever AI policy](c3). [The college posted the announcement on its faculty and staff news site {{date:c31}}](c31).

[The college's AI Resource Hub already links a document titled Acceptable Use of Artificial Intelligence Policy, posted for faculty and staff](c19). The post does not say whether the new policy replaces that document or sits beside it. [It describes the policy as in development and names no adoption date, no vote and no adopting body](c18).

paragraphs.text: [Two collegewide AI committees developed the framework, one for strategic planning and one for implementation](c4). Each of its rules is one sentence in the post.

[The first rule asks people to say so when AI plays a meaningful role in their work](c5). [Another asks them to check AI generated content carefully before they use or share it](c6). [The third says AI may support a person's work and should never replace their expertise, decision making or responsibility](c7). [One asks for honest work and real learning](c8). [The last asks for respect for copyright and for other people's creative work](c9).

[The college says more than {{number:c20}} students rely on it for their education each year](c20). [It says the October events are meant to gather community feedback and build capacity to discuss AI](c2). [It invites faculty, staff, students and community members to take part in one or more of them](c16).

[A Faculty and Student AI Town Hall is set for {{date:c10}} at the Rio Grande Campus](c10). [The college says it will cover in-progress AI policies](c11). [A faculty convocation titled The Two AIs](c12) [meets {{date:c13}} at the Eastview Campus](c13). [A community seminar on {{date:c14}} at the Highland Campus is a guided discussion of E. M. Forster's story The Machine Stops](c14). [The seminar is open to community members](c15). [Feedback and questions go through a form on the college's page about getting involved with generative AI](c17).

[The post names no adoption date, no vote and no adopting body](c18). [The college's AI site already carries a use policy written for faculty and staff](c19). A reader of the post can't tell who decides between the two documents or when.

[In a post {{date:c21}} UT Austin said new partnerships with Anthropic and OpenAI make Claude EDU and ChatGPT EDU available](c21). [It says it provides both to its entire community at no cost](c22). [Richardson ISD's draft legislative priorities list the responsible use of technology and AI first](c29). [Its board is expected to vote on them {{date:c30}}](c30). [KFOX14 reported that an El Paso ISD draft framework would bar students through eighth grade from using AI to complete schoolwork](c27).
